# 2 Clement — Chapter 1 (LOGOS Formal)

**Source:** Codex Alexandrinus, 2 Clement 1
**Agent:** LOGOS (Formal Equivalence)
**Date:** 2026-03-17

---

1. Brothers, we must think of Jesus Christ as of God — as judge of the living and the dead. And we must not think lightly of our salvation.
2. For when we think lightly of him, we also expect to receive little. And those who listen as though they are receiving little things do wrong — we ourselves do wrong, not knowing from where and by whom and to what place we have been called, and how great things Jesus Christ willingly suffered for our sake.
3. What repayment, therefore, shall we render to him, or what fruit worthy of what he himself gave to us?
4. For how many holy things did we owe to him! He gave us the light; as a father he called us children; he saved us when we were perishing.
5. What praise, then, shall we give him, or what repayment in return for what we received? We were impaired in understanding, worshiping stones and wood and gold and silver and bronze — works of human hands; and our entire life was nothing other than death.
6. Being wrapped about in darkness and having our eyesight full of such mist, we recovered our sight, putting off by his will the cloud that covered us.
7. For he had mercy upon us, and, being moved with compassion, he saved us; beholding in us great error and destruction, and perceiving that we had no hope of salvation apart from him.
8. For he called us who were not in existence, and he willed us to come into being out of nothingness.
